assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos opened neutrino astronomy as an observational field. It required a kilometre-scale instrument built in Antarctic ice, with a clear measurement and a new window on cosmic-ray accelerators. Later evidence for TXS 0506+056 and for neutrinos from the Galactic plane strengthens the case.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube project over decades, and the supplied credit names him alone. A single laureate is a clean configuration, but IceCube is a large collaboration whose instrument builders and analysts (for example on the diffuse-flux and source analyses) are not on this list. I cannot verify from the supplied text how the committee would handle that breadth of credit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed repeatedly with independent analysis channels, and source associations have continued to accumulate. Recognition is timely: the discovery is well over a decade old and the field is established. Individual source identifications are less settled than the diffuse flux.
uncertainties: Whether a single named laureate fairly represents a project of this scale.
The origin of most of the diffuse flux remains unresolved, so the prize would reward the discovery and instrument rather than a full astrophysical interpretation.
Credit for the early AMANDA/IceCube concept and for other leaders is not resolved by the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring the last neutrino mixing angle theta-13 as unexpectedly large was a precision reactor experiment with consequences for the search for leptonic CP violation and for mass-ordering studies. It follows naturally from the 2015 prize for neutrino oscillations and is a clear, quantitative result.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) are credited, and the two reactor measurements were competitive and mutually confirming. Double Chooz and the accelerator T2K hint also contributed and are not on this list, so the prize configuration is arguable. The three listed names are a reasonable representation of the decisive reactor results.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several experiments and now a precisely known parameter that is built into global fits. The discovery dates to 2012 and is mature; recognition is slightly delayed but not premature.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Daya Bay, RENO and Double Chooz, and between collaboration leaders and key analysts.
Whether the committee regards the result as a measurement of a parameter rather than a discovery of a new phenomenon after the 2015 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials. It combines a clear theoretical prediction with a striking experimental discovery and has widespread impact across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key prediction in 2011 and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations. This theory-plus-experiment configuration is a natural fit. Other experimental groups (for example Dean and collaborators on related moire systems) and the Cao co-first-author contributions raise allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups and extended to many moire platforms within a few years. The field is still developing quickly, and some interpretations of the superconducting mechanism are unsettled, so recognition would be somewhat early but well supported.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are not settled.
Credit for other experimental and theoretical contributors to moire physics is not captured by three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength trapping concept, gave a new generation of frequency standards with fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It supports tests of fundamental physics and is a candidate for redefining the second. This is a precision-measurement achievement of high significance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Ye led the demonstration of its best performance. The two names form a clear and plausible configuration. Other clock groups and the ion-clock community are outside this candidate, and the earlier work on frequency combs and ion clocks has been recognised already.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories operate lattice clocks and compare them at high precision. The achievement is mature, while the formal redefinition of the second has not yet happened, which does not by itself undermine the physics.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior prizes for frequency combs and for ion trapping, and how the committee judges novelty relative to them.
Whether strontium and ytterbium lattice contributions of other groups need to be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provided the architecture for controlling and reading out superconducting qubits and made strong light-matter coupling accessible on a chip. It underpins current superconducting quantum processors and has had lasting influence on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Wallraff and Schoelkopf are credited; the theory proposal and the first experimental demonstration are separable contributions. I choose three, keeping the experimental demonstration (Wallraff, Schoelkopf) together with the main theoretical proposal (Blais), but Girvin's role is also strong and this selection is contestable. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is related and complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently reproduced across many laboratories. The architecture is mature even though the technological payoff of quantum computing is still unfolding.
uncertainties: Proximity to the recently awarded superconducting-circuit work may count against novelty.
Fair division among four credited people with an essential theory-experiment split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP made high-precision full-sky measurements of the cosmic microwave background and established the standard Lambda-CDM parameters to percent level. As an experimentalist I value that it was a space-borne instrument whose systematics control (the differencing design and the cold, stable orbit) made the results credible. It follows earlier CMB prizes, which does reduce novelty.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page led key instrument and calibration work, and Spergel led much of the cosmological analysis and interpretation. This is a sensible three-person configuration. David Wilkinson, a principal figure, died in 2002, and the broader team and the COBE and Planck contributions complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and surpassed by Planck, which supports the results strongly. This is mature and perhaps overdue, but the 2006 and 2019 awards raise the question of whether another cosmology prize adds enough.
uncertainties: Novelty relative to the 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Because Planck gave better precision, the committee may prefer to credit a discovery rather than a measurement.
Allocation to a large collaboration is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS detectors were the instruments that made the 2012 Higgs boson discovery possible and have since produced a large body of precision measurements. The instrumentation achievement is large in scale and in ingenuity, and as an instrument builder I regard it as worthy. The Higgs prize in 2013 went to the theorists, so this would recognise the experimental side.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee were founding spokespersons and architects of the proposals and designs. They are an appropriate three, but thousands of collaborators contributed, and the discovery announcement credit is shared across both experiments and across the accelerator at CERN. The Nobel statutes make an instrument-focused award tricky to define.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is confirmed with large data sets, but the existence of the 2013 prize and the wish to award a discovery, not a facility, may create a tension about timing and scope.
uncertainties: Whether the award is for detectors or for the discovery, and how to treat the LHC machine builders.
Fairness to other leaders such as the experiment spokespersons at the time of discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a bandstructure-engineered semiconductor laser that made mid-infrared and terahertz sources practical. It was an invention with clear originality and has a wide range of uses in sensing and spectroscopy, which is consistent with the Nobel emphasis on inventions of great benefit.
assessment.attribution: Faist and Capasso were the lead inventors and demonstrators at Bell Labs in 1994, with Cho providing the molecular-beam-epitaxy growth. The credited names include Cho, but I have restricted the list to two to keep the principal conceptual and device contributions. Cho's contribution is crucial and might merit inclusion, which I cannot resolve from the supplied text. Other team members and Kazarinov and Suris (who proposed the earlier idea) are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: The device is commercially established and widely used, with decades of independent confirmation. It is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Role of Cho and the earlier Kazarinov-Suris proposal in the priority claim.
Whether device invention in this area is competing with fundamental discoveries in the committee's priorities.
